questions.front: What kind of function is graphed here?
questions.back: A quadratic — $y = x^2$. Its graph is a parabola opening upward, symmetric about the $y$-axis.
One full cycle: up to $1$ at $\pi/2$, back through zero at $\pi$, down to $-1$ at $3\pi/2$.

questions.front: An object falls from rest. What does its velocity-time graph look like?
questions.back: A straight line through the origin with slope $g \approx 9.8$ m/s$^2$ — velocity grows linearly with time.
$KE = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$ — no graph on this card, so it should look exactly like an ordinary flashcard.

questions.front: Broken-graph fallback test — this samples $\sqrt{x}$ across negative $x$
questions.back: The plot should read "Graph unavailable" and the card should still flip normally.

questions.front: A long front with a graph — does the text still fit under the plot when it runs to more than a single line of card copy?
questions.back: Yes: the graph takes the leftover flex track and the text keeps its own line at the reduced caption size.
